canonicalFacts.claim: Chronic kidney disease affects approximately 850 million cases globally with 4 million individuals needing kidney replacement therapy
CKD is projected to become the fifth leading underlying cause of death worldwide by 2050
Hypertension and diabetes are the two most common etiologies of chronic kidney disease in the United States
CKD patients are at increased risk of premature cardiovascular disease, with most patients dying from cardiovascular causes rather than progressing to kidney failure
Combination therapy targeting multiple mechanisms is becoming a new standard of care for CKD

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Dietary modifications including low-protein and gluten-free diets can modulate microbial diversity and improve renal biomarkers
Prebiotics such as resistant starch have been shown to lower uremic toxins and reduce inflammation

redFlags: CKD patients remain asymptomatic most of the time, presenting complications only in advanced stages
CKD patients have significantly increased mortality risk with COVID-19 infection
Denosumab discontinuation increases risk of multiple vertebral fractures in CKD patients

pipelineDrugs.name: Runcaciguat
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Soluble guanylate cyclase activator that restores cGMP production

pipelineDrugs.name: Molidustat
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor with erythropoietic effects

excludedAgents.name: Febuxostat
excludedAgents.reason: Randomized controlled trial in 467 patients with stage 3 CKD and asymptomatic hyperuricemia showed no significant benefit on the primary endpoint of eGFR slope over 108 weeks

excludedAgents.name: Lactobacillus paracasei N1115
excludedAgents.reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial in peritoneal dialysis patients showed probiotic treatment induced changes in intestinal microbiota but did not alter SCFA levels

excludedAgents.name: Ziritaxestat
excludedAgents.reason: Phase 3 ISABELA 1 and 2 trials in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis were terminated early due to lack of efficacy, with follow-up completed early due to study termination
